To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the positioning of nucleosomes near CTCF binding site is inversely related to the binding strength and that nucleosome positioning patterns are characteristic of different cell types and can be used for diagnostic purposes.
CTCF binds to chromatin boundaries where nucleosome arrays are ordered and short, and that nucleosome positioning patterns can be used as diagnostic markers of cancer.
the nucleosome positioning and the 3D chromosomal organization are important determinants of the accessibility of regulatory proteins to DNA and are affected by the cell state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of nucleosome positioning with the higher level of genome organization and its changes during cell development.
the interplay of nucleosome positioning, CTCF binding and 3D organization of chromatin in different cell types.
the role of nucleosomes in the 3D organization of the genome and their interplay with CTCF and other regulatory proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the positioning of nucleosomes and the 3D chromosomal architecture are highly dynamic during the cell transitions and the changes of these parameters are a result of a complex interplay between DNA, histones and other proteins.
nucleosome positioning is an important feature of the genome that can be used to distinguish different cell types and to predict the chromatin state.
this thesis provides a novel view on the relationship between CTCF binding, nucleosome positioning and higher level chromatin organisation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleosome positioning and the chromatin structure are dynamic, changing during cell development.
the chromatin architecture of the nucleus is a highly dynamic system, which is constantly changing during the cell cycle, differentiation, and development.
nucleosome positioning and higher order chromatin organization are important for the regulation of gene expression and cell identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chromatin state of the genome can be inferred from the nucleosome positioning pattern, and this information can be used to identify the disease-specific patterns.
the machine learning models trained on the nucleosome positioning data can be used to distinguish between different cell types and to classify samples based on the presence of disease.
machine learning can be used to classify nucleosome positioning patterns in order to identify chromatin states that may have a diagnostic or prognostic value.
